name: tracker-mcp
description: Ask Claude about your job-application tracker in Excel or CSV, and let it record what happened, with your confirmation.
long_description:
Point it at the spreadsheet where you keep your job applications. Claude can then answer "which follow-ups are due this week?", "what's the status with Acme?" or "which channel gets me the most replies?", and record what happened: "I applied to Globex via LinkedIn", "Initech rejected me".

On first start the server reads your headers and writes a small config next to the file (`<name>.tracker-mcp.toml`); Claude tells you what to check in it. Every write is shown to you first and needs your yes. The server makes a backup before each write, refuses to write while Excel has the file open, and can undo its last write.

This extension takes an .xlsx or .csv file. For a tracker in Google Sheets, set the server up as the README describes (a one-time Google sign-in from the command line).

tracker.title: Your tracker
tracker.description: The .xlsx or .csv file with your applications, one row each. Don't have one? Create an empty file in Excel with the headers Company, Role, Status, Applied on, Follow-up date, Notes.

tools.name: describe_tracker

tools.name: list_applications
tools.description: Filter applications by status, text or submit dates

tools.name: get_application
tools.description: Everything recorded for one application

tools.name: followups_due
tools.description: Follow-ups due soon, overdue first

tools.name: stale_applications
tools.description: Applications with no reply for N days

tools.name: summary

tools.name: funnel

tools.name: reply_times

tools.name: match_emails

tools.name: recent_writes

tools.description: Record a submission and plan the follow-up (asks you first)

tools.name: set_status

tools.name: log_followup

tools.name: reschedule_followup
tools.description: Move or drop a follow-up when nothing was sent (asks you first)

tools.name: edit_application
tools.description: Correct a field of one application: a date, a typo, the furthest stage (asks you first)
